goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:1 — Normalized hostnames have no uniqueness validation or database constraint, allowing conflicting duplicates that record_for_host selects nondeterministically.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows EmbeddableHost model at app/models/embeddable_host.rb with only a format validation on host, no uniqueness validation. The before_validation normalizes hosts by stripping http/https and paths. The record_for_host method uses .first to select a record, which would return nondeterministically if duplicates exist. The migration and controller also don't prevent duplicates. This is a real defect - duplicate hosts could be created and the system would behave unpredictably when looking up which category to use for embedding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2 — Validation permits host values containing ports, but record_for_host strips ports via URI#host, making such entries unable to authorize requests.

adjudication.rationale:
The finding identifies a real inconsistency in the code. Looking at the diff:

1. In `app/models/embeddable_host.rb` line 2, the validation regex explicitly allows ports: `/\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\/i` - the `(:[0-9]{1,5})?` part permits port numbers.

2. The `before_validation` block (lines 5-8) strips the protocol and path but NOT the port from the host.

3. However, in `record_for_host` (lines 10-17), it uses `uri.host` which returns only the hostname WITHOUT the port. So if someone saves 'example.com:8080' as an embeddable host, when checking if 'http://example.com:8080/page' is allowed, `uri.host` returns 'example.com', which won't match 'example.com:8080' in the database.

This is a legitimate bug where the validation allows ports but the lookup logic cannot match them.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:37 — Saving a host without a category overwrites the server-defaulted Uncategorized category with findById(null), leaving the row without a displayed category until reload.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the save action in embeddable-host.js.es6 lines 29-38, after a successful save it calls `host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')))`. The categoryId is initialized to null (line 9) and only set in the edit action (line 25) from an existing host's category. For a new host where no category is explicitly selected, categoryId remains null. The server defaults to uncategorized_category_id (line 24 of embeddable_hosts_controller.rb), but the client-side code will call findById(null) which likely returns undefined/null, overwriting the server's default category assignment in the local model until reload.
